project_comments.note: Cross-cutting pattern: local $dom = str_get_html(...) with manual $dom->clear() appears in WP-003 (ReaderElementTest), WP-004 (ReaderSelectorTest), and WP-005 (InvalidHtmlTest). The root cause is that str_get_html() needs non-default parameters (e.g. 'UTF-8', false) that cannot be pre-set in setUp(). If an assertion fails before clear(), the DOM object is never freed. Recommended fix: assign the result to $this->dom each time (replace constructor call in setUp if flags differ per-test, or just do '$this->dom = str_get_html(...)' and remove all manual clear() calls — tearDown() handles it). A single cleanup pass across all three files would eliminate the pattern.

Architecture insight from WP-006 review: The simple_html_dom library has a silent content-loss bug where strings containing '<1 ...' (less-than followed by a digit) are parsed as broken tag openers and content after them is discarded. The legacy assert() suite was masking this because PHP assert() was not configured to throw. A follow-up WP should either (a) fix the library's tag-detection heuristic for numeric lookahead, or (b) add a 'Known Limitations' section to the README documenting this edge case so downstream consumers are not surprised.

Synthesis complete. Key cross-cutting findings: (1) Silent content-loss bug: strings containing '<digit' pattern (e.g. '<1 mol%') trigger broken-tag-opener detection, silently discarding all trailing content. This was masked in the legacy suite because PHP assert() was not configured to throw. Now surfaced and documented in StandardTest::testChemistryFormula. Recommend a dedicated WP to fix the heuristic or document it as a known limitation. (2) Local $dom teardown pattern (DOM leak on assertion failure) affects MiscTest, ReaderElementTest, ReaderSelectorTest, InvalidHtmlTest — a single cleanup pass would close this across all four files. (3) PHP 8.4+ $http_response_header deprecation in src/simple_html_dom.php (lines 99, 102, 113, 120) fires on every test run — recommend a PHP 9 readiness WP. (4) phpunit.xml has no <source> element — coverage reporting will be empty until added.
